points.text: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far designated his eldest son, Ali (known as Ali al-Akbar), as his immediate successor and Imam after his death.
Ali ibn Musa is described as possessing the authority, speech, writing, and messenger of his father, serving as his testamentary trustee (Wasi).
The Imamate will not cease with the death of Musa ibn Ja'far, but will continue through his son Ali and subsequently to his son Muhammad.
Ali ibn Musa is characterized by specific spiritual and historical attributes, including understanding, forbearance, and a connection to the lineage of Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ali ibn al-Husayn.
The succession is confirmed by the transfer of debts, promises, and wealth from the father to the son, establishing the son's authority over the father's affairs.
The Imamate is an unbroken chain that continues until the Day of Judgment, ensuring the community is never without an Imam.
Ali ibn Musa is identified as the Qaim (the active leader) and Hujjah (Divine Proof) who will succeed his father and maintain the religious authority.
